hook: In Seoul, buying a home takes your savings and a large loan, and the choice is often made after one short viewing. What if you could live there first?
pitch: Ithaca is a pre-living agent. An AI household lives thirty days in the homes you pick, before you buy.
ask: Here, a couple who both work in Pangyo type their situation in English: two salaries, two hundred million won saved, a home under seven hundred million. Muse Spark one point three reads it, and calls real tools.
candidates: The candidates come from the government's real purchase records, one per neighbourhood, each with the door-to-door commute to Pangyo.
live: Pick two. Muse lives thirty days in each home, with the same household and the same random seed. There's no ranking, and no winner.
days: Every trip is simulated minute by minute: real walking paths, subway timetables, and measured crowding. Each leg says whether it's measured or assumed.
results: After thirty days, you see the cost to buy, what you pay every month, and the real commute: seven minutes from one home, twenty-five from the other.
pay: Every won is itemised: the loan payment each month, and the acquisition tax, local education tax, rural development tax and agent fee, each with the law it comes from.
verify: Muse writes the report. Code re-checks every number, and every moment opens the three-D view at the minute it happened.
meta: Ithaca is built with Meta AI. Muse Spark one point three talks with you and makes the household's choices. Spark Open made the same choice in eighty-six percent of shared decisions. And Muse Code wrote every line of product code.
end: We walk the odyssey. You just come home.
